name: How do I modernize a bungalow or mid-century home without ruining the style?

mainEntity.name: What should be preserved when modernizing a bungalow, Spanish-style home, or mid-century house in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should be preserved when modernizing a bungalow, Spanish-style home, or mid-century house in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Style-sensitive modernization is usually what gives older Los Angeles homes the best long-term value. A bungalow, Spanish-style house, or mid-century home has proportions and details that should guide the remodel. The important elements to preserve are the roofline, window rhythm, trim profiles, ceiling character, built-ins, material palette, and the relationship between indoor and outdoor spaces. Modernizing does not mean making the house look new in a generic way. It means improving function, light, storage, and comfort while respecting the architecture that made the home desirable in the first place. That often requires restraint: keep the best original features, upgrade the mechanical systems, and use new elements that feel compatible instead of loud. The strongest remodels look intentional because they are rooted in the home’s style rather than imposed on top of it.
acceptedAnswer.description: Preserve the proportions, rooflines, openings, trim details, and signature materials that define the style. Modernization should improve comfort, flow, and systems while keeping the home’s original architectural language intact. The best projects upgrade function without flattening the style into something generic.
